In **BA_2025_10K.pdf** - Boeing 2025 Form 10-K - the filing gives the following for **IAM District 837 / IAM 837**:

### 1. The 2025 strike / work stoppage - p.4, p.11-12, p.26

The filing describes the same event in three places:

**Human Capital, p.4:**
> *employees represented by IAM District 837, which represents **approximately 3,200 employees at our St. Louis area sites**, went out on strike for **101 days**, disrupting our St. Louis operations and impacting programs including **F/A-18, F-15, T-7A, MQ-25 and Weapons**.*

**Item 1A. Risk Factors, p.11-12:**
> *employees represented by IAM District 837, which represents **approximately 3,200 employees at our St. Louis area sites**, went out on strike for **101 days**, disrupting our St. Louis operations and impacting programs including F/A-18, F-15, T-7A, MQ-25 and Weapons.*

**Item 7. MD&A - Overview, p.26:**
> *On **November 13, 2025**, the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers District 837 (IAM 837), representing **approximately 3,200 Boeing employees**, voted to **ratify a new contract thereby ending the work stoppage initiated on August 4, 2025**, which disrupted our St. Louis operations.*

What each refers to:

* **approximately 3,200** - employee count represented by IAM District 837 at St. Louis area sites. P.26 phrases as *approximately 3,200 Boeing employees* covered by IAM 837. This is the bargaining unit that struck.
* **101 days** - duration of the 2025 strike/work stoppage.
* **August 4, 2025** - initiation date of the work stoppage.
* **November 13, 2025** - date of ratification vote for new contract, thereby ending the work stoppage. P.11 notes both the 2024 IAM 751 and 2025 IAM 837 strikes occurred despite tentative agreement and union leadership recommendation to ratify.

### 2. Current collective bargaining agreement with IAM District 837 - p.4

**Human Capital table - Principal collective bargaining agreements, p.4:**

* **Union:** The International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers (IAM) - **25% of Total Workforce**
* **Major Agreement:** **IAM District 837**
* **Principal Location: Missouri** - text elsewhere clarifies **St. Louis area sites**
* **Expiration Date: July 2030**

This is listed as the current principal agreement with IAM District 837, covering the same ~3,200-employee St. Louis unit. P.26 indicates the new contract ratified November 13, 2025 ending the strike is the contract that now expires July 2030.

For context the filing reports as of December 31, 2025: total workforce **approximately 182,000**, of which **approximately 72,000** or **40%** were union represented under 32 U.S. agreements with 9 unions.

> **$345 million per year - Risk Factors p.19:**
> 
> `we expect to require up to $345 million of cash per year for the payment of dividends on the outstanding shares of our 6.00% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock ... through the mandatory conversion date of October 15, 2027`
>
> This is the forward-looking maximum annual cash requirement disclosure in `Item 1A. Risk Factors`. $345M = 5.75M shares × $1,000 × 6.00%. Dividends accumulate at 6.00% per annum on $1,000 liquidation preference, payable when, as and if declared by Board in cash and/or common stock. Any unpaid dividends continue to accumulate.

The filing then reports two different historical amounts for the stub period in 2024 from issuance 10/31/2024 to 12/31/2024:

> **$58 million - Accumulated during the period - 2024:**
>
> * Consolidated Statements of Operations p.56: `Less: Mandatory convertible preferred stock dividends accumulated during the period 58` - in $ millions - deducted from `Net loss attributable to Boeing shareholders ($11,817)` to arrive at `Net loss attributable to Boeing common shareholders ($11,875)`
> * Summary of Business Segment Data p.63: same line `58`
> * Note 4 Earnings Per Share p.77: `Net loss attributable to Boeing shareholders ($11,817) Less: Mandatory convertible preferred stock dividends accumulated during the period 58 = Net loss available to common shareholders ($11,875)` for two-class method basic/diluted EPS calculation. Years ended 12/31/2023 and 2022 = 0.

This is the GAAP accrual for EPS purposes for the portion of the dividend period that elapsed in 2024, even if not yet declared/paid.

> **$72 million - Declared in December 2024 - p.62 and Note 19 p.110:**
>
> * Consolidated Statements of Equity p.62: `Cash dividends declared on Mandatory convertible preferred stock (72)` - $ millions - reduction of Retained earnings / Total equity in 2024 rollforward. Balance at 12/31/2024.
> * Note 19 Shareholders' Equity - Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock p.110: `In December 2024, dividends of $72 were declared to holders of record as of January 1, 2025, representing $12.50 per share, and were paid in cash on January 15, 2025.`
>
> Dividends are cumulative at 6.00% on $1,000 per share, payable quarterly Jan 15, Apr 15, Jul 15, Oct 15 to holders of record Jan 1, Apr 1, Jul 1, Oct 1.

> **$12.50 per share - Per-share amount of that declaration - p.110:**
>
> $72M ÷ 5.75M outstanding preferred shares = $12.50 per share declared in Dec 2024 for Jan 15 2025 payment. Text explicitly: `representing $12.50 per share`.

No dividends were accumulated or declared for 2023 or 2022, as the stock was issued 10/31/2024.

* **Referred** Company to U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of California for determination whether **criminal contempt proceedings** are appropriate.

**4. October 2025 - Epic Games appeal:**

On January 1, 2023 adoption of ASU 2022-02 **Financial Instruments - Credit Losses: Troubled Debt Restructurings ("TDRs")** - **modified retrospective method** - JPMorgan Chase & Co. 2023 Form 10-K discloses:

**Allowance impact - pre-tax, at January 1, 2023:**

> *resulted in a net decrease to the allowance for credit losses of $ 587 million* [p.175][p.258] and *allowance for credit losses also reflected a reduction of $587 million as a result of the adoption* [p.133][p.262]

The Form 10-K identifies this as the **allowance for loan losses - cumulative effect of a change in accounting principle** [p.260][p.134]:

* Total Firm - allowance for loan losses / allowance for credit losses: **- $587 million** - net decrease to total allowance for loan losses (allowance for lending-related commitments = NA, so same as total allowance for credit losses)
* Consumer, excluding credit card - allowance for loan losses: **- $489 million** - decrease, *predominantly driven by residential real estate* [p.175][p.258]
* Credit card - allowance for loan losses: **- $100 million** - decrease, *predominantly driven by credit card* [p.175][p.258]
* Wholesale - allowance for loan losses: **+ $2 million** - increase
  * Table: (489) / (100) / 2 / (587) [p.260][p.134] = Net **$587 million decrease**.

Firm elected to change from asset-specific DCF approach to non-DCF portfolio-based approach for modified loans to troubled borrowers except collateral-dependent and nonaccrual risk-rated loans [p.258].

**Retained earnings impact - after-tax, at January 1, 2023:**

> *increase to retained earnings of $ 446 million, after-tax* [p.175][p.258] - cumulative-effect adjustment to opening retained earnings on adoption, *predominantly driven by residential real estate and credit card* [p.175][p.258].

All amounts in **millions of dollars**.

$774 million + ~$1.4 billion ≈ $2.2 billion total provision.
